author: AmonStrix
quote: GTA VI: Beautiful Graphics, But Where Did the Freedom Go? Let’s be completely honest: GTA VI feels like the same old formula—another GTA with a different story, but nothing groundbreaking. After all the hype, several issues are hard to ignore. Missing classic features: No prostitutes? Something that has existed in GTA for decades is suddenly gone. Why remove features that were part of the franchise’s identity? Forced “woke” elements: The game feels increasingly focused on pushing certain messages instead of simply letting players enjoy themselves. It’s exhausting.Where did the freedom go? This is my biggest complaint. You can’t even attack or kill every NPC anymore. Some characters appear to be protected, including certain gay characters and women, while others aren’t. Why the double standards? I don’t care about an NPC’s gender or sexual orientation. The same gameplay rules should apply to **** was always about freedom, chaos, and doing whatever you wanted in a fictional world. That was the entire point! Now we’re getting restrictions on who we can attack and what we can do. What’s the point of a massive open world if the game constantly limits your choices? Apparently, we can smoke cigarettes, sit on benches, and enjoy countless realistic animations, but we can’t experience the unrestricted sandbox gameplay that made GTA **** I’m tired of being Lucia’s lapdog. Seriously, I’m sick of feeling like Jason is constantly playing the submissive boyfriend, following Lucia around and doing whatever she wants. If I wanted that kind of relationship dynamic, I could experience it in real life. I didn’t spend $90 on GTA to play a boyfriend simulator. I want crime, chaos, action, and freedom—not a relationship where I’m constantly taking orders.30 FPS in 2026 is unacceptable: I don’t care how gorgeous the graphics are. Being locked to 30 FPS on PS5 Pro is ridiculous. Not even a 60 FPS performance mode? Worse, I’ve experienced drops to 15–18 FPS in certain areas. How is that acceptable in a $90 AAA game?Clunky physics and missing details: Character movement and physics feel poorly tuned. Even basic immersion details, like animations for putting on or removing a helmet, are missing.Realism is hurting the experience: Visually, GTA VI is absolutely stunning. But Rockstar seems so obsessed with realism that it sometimes forgets what makes a game enjoyable. More animations, more environmental details, more activities—but less freedom where it actually matters.I played it on my PS5 Pro and eventually dropped it. Playing at 30 FPS on an 80-inch 240Hz TV looks terrible. Maybe it feels acceptable on older displays, but on modern high-end hardware, it’s disappointing.Hopefully, the eventual PC version will finally let us enjoy 60 FPS or even 150 FPS with an RTX 5090 and DLSS 5, assuming the technology and optimization allow it. And hopefully, the physics improve **** performance isn’t even my biggest disappointment. It’s the loss of GTA’s identity.I don’t need a beautiful open world where I can sit on a bench, smoke cigarettes, and admire realistic scenery while the game constantly tells me what I can and cannot do.I don’t want to be Lucia’s personal lapdog, either. I WANT GRAND THEFT AUTO. I WANT CHAOS. I WANT FUN. I WANT FREEDOM. It’s a video game, not real life. It’s supposed to let us escape real-world restrictions and enjoy a fictional sandbox without unnecessary limitations. Rockstar gave us a bigger, prettier world, but somehow made it feel smaller by taking away the freedom that made GTA legendary. And that’s the biggest disappointment of all.

author: AmonStrix
quote:
Castlevania: Belmont's Curse — Nintendo Switch Review — 9/10

Castlevania is finally back, and it's embracing the evolution of the genre it helped create.Games like Hollow Knight, Silksong, Nine Sols, Blasphemous, and Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown have spent years improving the foundations established by Castlevania and Metroid. Now, Castlevania takes those modern ideas and combines them with its own legacy, delivering an excellent action-exploration experience.This isn't a generic Metroidvania copying other games. 

This is Castlevania evolving alongside a genre it helped define. The gameplay, exploration, and overall design capture what made the franchise special while introducing modern mechanics.However, my biggest complaint with the Nintendo Switch version is the lack of a dedicated Nintendo Switch 2 edition. 

A native Switch 2 release with a 120 FPS performance mode would be fantastic, especially for a game where fluid movement, precise combat, and responsiveness matter so much. This franchise deserves that level of optimization on Nintendo's latest hardware.I'd also improve the fast-travel system and add more of those classic dark, gothic musical themes that made Castlevania unforgettable.Despite these complaints, this is an excellent game that every Metroidvania fan should experience.

Don't let anyone convince you that this isn't Castlevania simply because it embraces modern gameplay mechanics. A legendary franchise doesn't lose its identity by evolving.Final Score: 9/10. Highly recommended! Just give us that native Nintendo Switch 2 version with 120 FPS support. Castlevania deserves it!

author: AmonStrix
quote:
Castlevania: Belmont's Curse — 9.5/10

A legendary franchise evolving alongside the genre it helped create.

For me, this game is easily a 9.5/10. What we have here is a Castlevania that takes everything that made the franchise great during its golden years and successfully adapts it to modern gameplay mechanics. 

And honestly, that's exactly what a new Castlevania should be. Games like Hollow Knight, Silksong, Nine Sols, Blasphemous, and Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown have spent years refining the foundations established by classics like Castlevania and Metroid. 

They introduced more fluid movement, refined combat, deeper exploration, and modern mechanics that pushed the genre forward. And that's exactly my point. For nearly 18 years, we hadn't seen a major new Castlevania following the traditional 2D exploration-focused formula. Meanwhile, other developers continued evolving the genre, often drawing inspiration from the very games that helped define it.

Now Castlevania is finally embracing those improvements and incorporating them into its own formula. That's not copying. 

That's evolution. This game combines elements from several successful modern Metroidvanias while preserving the foundations that made Castlevania special. 

You can recognize mechanics inspired by other games, but that doesn't automatically make the experience generic. Quite the opposite. Castlevania helped establish this genre, and now it's learning.

Regarding those who keep saying "This isn't Castlevania" or "This is just another generic Metroidvania," I strongly disagree. I'd genuinely be curious how many of those people have actually completed the last ten games in the franchise before making such statements. Castlevania has never been defined by just one formula. Compare Rondo of Blood, Symphony of the Night, Aria of Sorrow, and Order of Ecclesia. Each introduced different approaches to combat, exploration, progression, and gameplay. Yet they're all undeniably Castlevania. A franchise doesn't lose its identity simply because it evolves. And that's what I appreciate about this game. It combines familiar Castlevania elements with modern action-exploration mechanics while trying to establish its own identity rather than simply recreate something from twenty years ago. Of course, it's not perfect. One thing I'd improve is the fast-travel system and navigation between different map areas. I'd also love to see a dedicated Nintendo Switch 2 version. I played it on PC, and the graphical quality genuinely impressed me. The environments, visual presentation, and attention to detail are excellent. The soundtrack is another highlight, although I personally miss some of those darker, gothic, and mysterious compositions traditionally associated with Castlevania. I enjoyed the music overall, but I would have appreciated a little more of that classic atmosphere. Beyond those minor criticisms, I strongly recommend this game. If you enjoy search-action games or Metroidvanias, this absolutely deserves a place on your must-play list. And please, don't let people saying "This isn't Castlevania" or "It's just another generic Metroidvania" discourage you from playing it. Because they're missing the bigger picture. This isn't a generic Metroidvania pretending to be Castlevania. This is Castlevania adapting to the modern evolution of the very genre it helped define .It brings its own history, identity, and legacy into a modern action-exploration experience while embracing the innovations that have helped the genre grow over the past two decades. Not every returning franchise needs to reinvent the wheel. Sometimes, the smartest approach is to understand what made the originals special, recognize how gaming has evolved, and bring those ideas together into something meaningful. That's exactly what this game accomplishes for me.
